title: 1D Vibration - Eigenvalue Problem (FEM)
desc.equation: Free axial vibration of a bar: u(x, t) is the axial displacement, E(x) Young's modulus, ρ(x) the density and A(x) the cross-sectional area:
desc.eig: With u(x, t) = φ(x)·e^{iωt}, the discretization leads to the generalized eigenvalue problem, whose eigenvalues give the natural frequencies:
desc.props: E, ρ and A are constant or vary along x (linearly, parabolically or exponentially) according to the properties selector.
desc.domain: Bar of length L divided into nₑ linear elements of uniform size:
desc.bc.ff: Free-free (no constraint; the first mode is a rigid-body mode, with f = 0):
desc.bc.fixsup: Fixed-pinned (in the axial model, whose only degree of freedom is u, it coincides with fixed-fixed):
desc.method: Finite Element Method with linear bar elements: stiffness matrix and lumped mass matrix. Prescribed displacements imposed by the penalty method. Generalized eigenvalue problem solved by symmetric decomposition (scipy.linalg.eigh); the first 5 modes are normalized by their maximum amplitude.
desc.reference: Analytical natural frequencies for constant properties, with the axial wave speed
desc.reference.note: For variable properties or for the fixed-pinned case the simulation shows only the numerical result.
